tagline: Down Goose Lake and across the Modoc country to Tulelake.
intro: The map line starts up at Lakeview, but the byway itself begins at New Pine Creek on the Oregon line and comes south on US 395 past Goose Lake to Alturas, the Modoc county seat on the Pit River. There it turns west on Highway 299 to Canby, then northwest on Highway 139 over mostly flat ground through the middle of the Modoc National Forest to Tulelake.

Gold rush emigrants came this way on the Applegate-Lassen Cut-Off, which crossed the Black Rock Desert to Goose Lake. Northwest of Canby a state landmark marks a stretch of the old trail that can still be traced, with trees eight to ten inches thick growing in the road bed.

moments.title: New Pine Creek
moments.text: Oregon's southernmost town lies south of the 42nd parallel thanks to a surveying error of 1868, and talks between the two states in 1984 left it where it was.

moments.title: Goose Lake
moments.text: A large alkaline lake on the state line that has gone completely dry more than once since 1851, and in the high-water years around 1910 carried a ferry between Davis Creek and Lakeview.

moments.title: Canby
moments.text: Named for General Edward Canby, shot by Captain Jack at a peace parley in the Modoc War, the town is known for the nativity scenes along its main street, which is Highway 299.
